objective: Proof: Dehn filling parallel copies of the edge curves of the closed doubles along the slopes lambda mu^-p and lambda mu^p multiplies the anyon channel (flux lambda, charge psi) by |sum of psi over the p-th roots of lambda in C(lambda)|^2 / psi(1)^2, which vanishes on fluxes with no p-th root. If a finite group G has an abelian normal subgroup A of prime index p on whose p-th powers pA it acts nontrivially, then with fins interpolated and one doubled root filling per edge the surviving top channels are the free pairs of A inside pA x Ann(A[p]), and their coefficient is |G:pA| |A[p]| (|L'|/|A|)^|V| P(G,q) with q = |[pA,G]|^2 >= 4. With the trivial-action cases (all non-abelian anyons of dimension p; or, for p >= 3, the fluxes outside A) this proves #P-hardness for every group with an abelian normal subgroup of prime index, except possibly p = 2 with trivial action on 2A and |[A,G]| >= 4. In particular the dihedral group of order 16 (coefficient 8 P(G,4)/2^|V|) and every 2-power dihedral, semidihedral and generalized quaternion group of order at least 16. Hardness for all non-abelian groups already follows from Galindo's 2026 Turaev-Viro dichotomy; this is an independent elementary route with explicit chromatic coefficients. Standard-library checks.

The hardness itself already follows from Galindo's 2026 Turaev-Viro dichotomy; this is an independent elementary route with explicit chromatic coefficients.
title: Root fillings separate the order-16 collision
